findings.description: The user_data script contains plaintext AWS access key ID and secret access key. These are stored unencrypted in Terraform state and instance metadata, and are retrievable by anyone with EC2 API/console access or access to the instance metadata service, leading to credential leakage.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from any host on the internet.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF), increasing the attack surface for the web service to the entire internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on this volume is stored unencrypted and could be exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed improperly.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted EBS volume and has no encryption settings, so the snapshot data at rest is unencrypted and could be shared/exposed without protection.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing direct internet exposure of resources such as web_host.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instances launched in this subnet, expanding the internet-facing attack surface.
The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to network flow log data.
